advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the 'may predate' wording to the config read of the pinned snapshot that drift was proven against, not to every config read in the process after a drifted gate.
evidence: src/rebar/_config_coercion.py:64-66 wording is driven solely by the sticky global
src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:219-221 flag only re-evaluated on the next resolve_gate_handle, not scoped to the pinned-config read that motivated it
src/rebar/config.py:444 `Config.from_mapping(raw, source=str(p), strict=_strict_unknown_keys())` — config is read from many sites unrelated to a gate snapshot
advisory.finding: After a drifted gate sets `_BUILD_MAY_PREDATE_KEYS=True`, the flag stays True until the NEXT `resolve_gate_handle` flips it. Any config read done in the process between gates — including reads of the operator's LOCAL (non-snapshot) config — will render a genuine typo as 'this build may predate it', which is the opposite misdirection.
scenarios: A drifted gate runs, then a later unrelated code path reads the operator's local rebar.toml with an actual typo'd key

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_resolve_repo_root` return `None` on exception (or update the comment) so behavior matches the documented 'no repo root → no check' contract.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:141 comment: `# No resolvable repo root means no drift check.`
advisory.finding: `_resolve_repo_root` returns the raw `repo_root` argument on exception rather than `None`, contradicting its docstring ('No resolvable repo root means no drift check') and the module's stated 'degrade to silence' contract.
scenarios: `rebar.config.repo_root` raises while `repo_root` is a non-None but invalid path
advisory.suggested_fix: In the except branch, `return None` instead of `return repo_root`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting gate_source.resolve_gate_handle invokes build_drift.warn_if_behind with handle.sha (e.g. spy/monkeypatch on build_drift.warn_if_behind and assert it was called with the resolved handle's sha).
evidence: gate_source.py:109 `build_drift.warn_if_behind(handle.sha, repo_root)` is the sole production integration point introduced by this change
search of tests for `warn_if_behind` returns only tests/unit/test_build_drift.py — no test in tests/interfaces/*/*gate* or elsewhere asserts resolve_gate_handle calls it
ABSENCE: no test passes handle.sha through resolve_gate_handle and observes a warning / spy on build_drift.warn_if_behind, so the seam that makes the module actually run in a gate is regression-blind
advisory.finding: The new call site wiring build_drift into the gate flow (gate_source.resolve_gate_handle line 109 calling build_drift.warn_if_behind(handle.sha, repo_root)) has no test. All build_drift tests exercise the module in isolation; none assert that resolving a gate handle actually triggers the drift check, so removing or breaking line 109 would silently disable the entire feature with a fully green suite.
scenarios: A refactor of resolve_gate_handle drops or reorders the warn_if_behind call
A future change moves the call before acquire() so handle.sha is unavailable
advisory.suggested_fix: In an existing resolve_gate_handle integration test (or a new one), monkeypatch build_drift.warn_if_behind with a recording stub and assert it is called once with the resolved handle.sha after acquire().

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the build-drift wording flag gate-scoped (e.g. a ContextVar) rather than a process-global, to match use_code_root/use_tickets_root and avoid cross-gate races.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:221: `_note_config_wording(drift is not None)` set on EVERY resolution
src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py:218-227 use_code_root uses a ContextVar precisely so gate read-root is per-context not process-global
tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_source_threading.py exercises concurrent resolve_gate_handle, showing gates can run in parallel in one process
dropped.finding: `_BUILD_MAY_PREDATE_KEYS` is a process-global module variable mutated on every `resolve_gate_handle` call, but gate read-state elsewhere in this codebase is deliberately ContextVar-scoped (use_code_root/use_tickets_root). Under concurrent gate runs in one process, a non-drifted gate calling `_note_config_wording(False)` can clear the flag a drifted gate just set (or vice-versa) before the config read, making the unknown-key wording non-deterministic.
scenarios: Two gates (one behind the pinned ref, one at/ahead) resolving handles concurrently in the same server process
A fan-out workflow resolving multiple gate handles
